small_guidance:
- The GEMM is M=128, N=16384, K=16384 — M is tiny, so BLOCK_M=32 or 16 is sufficient; bias toward BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=4 configs and drop the large-BLOCK_M configs. Add a GROUP_M swizzle (e.g. 8) for L2 reuse across N tiles.
- The 3-pass softmax re-reads the row 3× from HBM (128×16384×4B = 8MB per row × 3). Switch to a persistent single-pass online softmax: keep tiles resident in registers across passes by using one program per row with BLOCK_SIZE=16384 (full row fits with num_warps=16, ~64KB per row in regs/SMEM) and do max+sum online, then normalize from the kept tile.
- Fuse the bias add and (in eval) the softmax into the GEMM epilogue is impractical due to row reduction across N tiles, but you can fuse the row-max reduction into the GEMM by writing partial (tile_max, tile_sumexp) per N-tile and combining; or simpler, just drop the 3rd pass by caching exp values via a larger BLOCK_SIZE.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a fused GEMM+softmax: since M=128 is tiny, launch one program per output row that streams the full K=16384 dot product for all N=16384 columns in N-tile chunks, accumulating into an online-softmax state (running max m, running sum s, and either a register-resident row or a single stored row). This eliminates the intermediate 128×16384 writeback and the 3-pass softmax reread — currently ~24MB of HBM traffic just for softmax.
- Alternative: split-K GEMM with one program per (row, N-tile), store the full logits row, then a separate fast online-softmax kernel that does max+sum in one pass (cache exp in SRAM if it fits, else two passes). With N=16384 and fp32, a full row is 64KB — too big for full SRAM cache, so two-pass with better tiling (BLOCK_SIZE=8192, num_warps=32) is the practical fallback.
- Consider fp16/bf16 accumulation path: cast weights to bf16 once at init (keeping the op intact — still a full GEMM) to roughly halve K-loop memory traffic, since this workload is memory-bound on the 4090 at K=16384.
